newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong to remain vital to Britain -Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to remain vital to Britain -Rifkind.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, beginning a week-long trip to south-east Asia, said on Wednesday that Hong Kong will remain "of vital importance" to Britain after the territory's handover to China at the end of June.
In a speech in Singapore, the text of which was released in London, Rifkind said: "At the midnight stroke on June 30, Britain's relationship with Hong Kong will change...But it will not end."
"For Britain, as for so many other countries in this region and beyond, Hong Kong will remain of vital importance, as a gateway to China and as an economic and financial centre," he said.

Rifkind, in Singapore for ministerial meetings between the Association of South-East Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the European Union, is due to meet Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen on Friday. He will then go on to Hong Kong for a three-day visit.

Britain and China have clashed repeatedly on Hong Kong, with London being particularly critical of what it claims are Beijing's undemocratic plans to set up a new legislative council in what is at present a British colony.
"Our deep commitment to Hong Kong will remain, as a matter of political and moral obligation to Hong Kong people, to the three million who still hold British passports," Rifkind said.
About half the British colony's population hold passports as British Dependent Territory Citizens. But these documents confer no right to live in Britain.
Rifkind said Britain would want to ensure that the joint agreement with China under which Hong Kong is to continue as a separate territory for 50 years is fully implemented.
He said that Britain had a deep economic relationship with Hong Kong, with 70 billion pounds ($114.4 billion) invested there.
